target_domain: Superheavy-element science concerned with the possible completion of the periodic table, including synthesis of elements beyond Z = 118, nuclear-stability prediction, single-atom chemical handling, and discovery verification.
core_gap: Existing methods do not provide an integrated, experimentally anchored way to determine whether future elements can be synthesized, survive long enough, be captured and chemically identified as single atoms, and satisfy discovery criteria. Hot-fusion reaction studies can propose candidate pathways, but quasifission, tiny cross sections, and survival uncertainties remain. Superheavy-nucleus theory must extrapolate nuclear interactions into poorly constrained regions, while chemical-transport simulations show that identification becomes a time-critical single-atom problem. The field therefore lacks a unified predictive and verifiable framework linking reaction choice, nuclear stability, decay observables, rapid chemical handling, and atomic-number assignment for elements beyond Z = 118.
